What it means: Growth in company sales. In this report it uses a proxy to show recent top-line momentum.
Measurement period used: TTM YoY proxy (latest 4 quarters vs prior 4 quarters). Refreshed at report run.

What it means: Growth in earnings per share, indicating profit growth per share.
Measurement period used: TTM YoY proxy (latest 4 reported EPS quarters vs prior 4). Refreshed at report run.

What it means: Operating profitability before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization.
Measurement period used: TTM margin from latest available fundamentals snapshot.

What it means: Net profit after all expenses as a share of revenue.
Measurement period used: TTM margin from latest available fundamentals snapshot.

What it means: Capital efficiency (returns generated on invested capital). If ROIC unavailable, ROE is used as fallback.
Measurement period used: Latest available annual/TTM-style field from provider snapshot.

What it means: Free cash flow generated per dollar of revenue.
Measurement period used: TTM FCF ÷ TTM/annualized revenue from latest snapshot.

What it means: Leverage ratio. Lower is generally safer; negative can imply net cash.
Measurement period used: Latest available balance-sheet and EBITDA snapshot.

What it means: Valuation based on expected next-year earnings. Lower may imply cheaper valuation (context-dependent).
Measurement period used: Forward estimate at report run; trailing P/E used only if forward unavailable.

What it means: Free cash flow relative to equity value (market cap). Higher can imply better cash return on price.
Measurement period used: TTM FCF ÷ market cap at report run.

What it means: Benchmark level used for ranges. Built from median of SPY top holdings metrics.
Measurement period used: Refreshed weekly; held constant for 7 days (see refresh/valid-until dates on page 1).
